sources.title: Stochastic Waveform Estimation at the Fundamental Quantum Limit

evidence.text: Analytic bounds use Uhlmann purification and parameter-dependent environment 'hiding' unitaries. Gaussian weak-signal criteria use Williamson decomposition; the general support/null-space criterion uses a channel Taylor expansion.

sources.title: Lindblad estimation with fast and precise quantum control

evidence.text: Use asymptotic unbiased estimation, classical/quantum Fisher information and Kraus-gauge channel bounds. An explicit gauge yields β̂=0 and an operator-norm optimization; minimax and purification convert this bound into optimization over initial states. Semidefinite programs supply numerical optima.

sources.title: Stochastic Waveform Estimation at the Fundamental Quantum Limit

evidence.text: Non-Gaussian probes are evaluated in truncated Fock spaces. Searches over sparse Fock superpositions use gradient descent and particle swarm optimization; an alternating convex search was also attempted without establishing global optimality.

sources.title: Stochastic Waveform Estimation at the Fundamental Quantum Limit

evidence.text: CFI, QFI, symmetric logarithmic derivatives and weak commutativity organize estimation bounds. Spectral-parameter QFIMs follow by chain rule and summing independent frequency contributions; arbitrary orthogonal temporal bases are also considered.

sources.title: Lindblad estimation with fast and precise quantum control

evidence.text: Gram–Schmidt orthogonalization places the initial state and its noise images before signal images, separating noisy and noise-free subspaces. Compute the projector using a Gram-matrix inverse or Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse when noise images are dependent. For commuting Hermitian jumps, optimization reduces to real vectors and probability distributions.

sources.title: The Size of a Soliton

evidence.text: The first subleading semiclassical expansion is evaluated with point splitting, a vacuum mass counterterm, and vacuum-energy subtraction. Coincidence limits are taken after divergent terms cancel because local energy-density moments, rather than only total energy, are required.

sources.title: The Size of a Soliton
